questions.prompt: Determine the slope of each segment from the rotation, then describe the pattern.

responses.label: Compared with the slope of AB, the slope after a 90° or 270° rotation is …
After a 180° rotation, the slope is …

hints: Slope = (change in y) ÷ (change in x). Every segment starts at the origin.
B′ = (−5, 8), so the slope of A′B′ is 8 ÷ (−5).
Compare the slope of AB with the slope after the 90° rotation: what happened to the fraction, and what happened to its sign?

options: change in x ÷ change in y

solutionReview.headline: Every segment runs from A, which stays at the origin, to B or its image, so its slope is rise ÷ run from (0, 0).
reasoning: Slope of AB: AB runs from A(0, 0) to B(8, 5) (the warm-up before this one), so its slope is (5 − 0) ÷ (8 − 0) = 5/8.
Slope of A′B′ (90°): a 90° counterclockwise turn about the origin sends (x, y) to (−y, x), so B(8, 5) goes to B′(−5, 8). The slope is (8 − 0) ÷ (−5 − 0) = −8/5.
Slope of A″B″ (180°): a 180° turn about the origin sends (x, y) to (−x, −y), so B(8, 5) goes to B″(−8, −5). The slope is (−5 − 0) ÷ (−8 − 0) = 5/8.
Slope of A‴B‴ (270°): a 270° counterclockwise turn about the origin sends (x, y) to (y, −x), so B(8, 5) goes to B‴(5, −8). The slope is (−8 − 0) ÷ (5 − 0) = −8/5.
After a 90° or 270° rotation: flip 5/8 to 8/5 and change its sign, and you get −8/5, the slope of A′B′ and of A‴B‴. So the slope is the negative reciprocal. Check: (5/8) × (−8/5) = −1.
After a 180° rotation: A″B″ has slope 5/8, just as AB does, so the slope is the same.
solutionReview.answerSummary: AB and A″B″ have slope 5/8; A′B′ and A‴B‴ have slope −8/5. A 90° or 270° rotation gives the negative reciprocal, and a 180° rotation keeps the same slope.

steps.title: Theorem
steps.instruction: If two lines are perpendicular, their slopes are negative reciprocals: m₁ = −1/m₂, so m₁·m₂ = −1 (neither line vertical).

steps.title: Counterclockwise version
steps.instruction: Rotating R(a, b) 90° counterclockwise gives D(−b, a), so m₂ = a/(−b) and m₁ = b/a = −1/m₂.

steps.title: Rise over run
steps.instruction: Slope = rise ÷ run. A horizontal line has a rise of 0, so its slope is 0 ÷ run = 0. A vertical line has a run of 0, and division by 0 is undefined.

questions.prompt: The lines ${{A}}x+{{B}}y={{C1}}$ and $px {{q|signed}}y={{C2}}$ are perpendicular, where $p$ is a constant. What is the value of $p$?

optionRationales.${{p}}$: With this value the two slopes multiply to −1, so the lines are perpendicular.
optionRationales.${{dNoNegative}}$: This has the right size but the wrong sign: with it the two slopes multiply to 1, not −1.
optionRationales.${{dWrongCoefficient}}$: With this value the second line has slope 1, and 1 times the first slope is not −1.
optionRationales.${{dParallel}}$: With this value the second line has slope −1, and the two slopes multiply to a positive number, not −1.

solutionReview.headline: Use the product of the slopes.
reasoning: The first line has slope -{{A}}/{{B}}; the second has slope -p/{{q}}.
For perpendicular lines their product is -1, which gives p={{p}}.
solutionReview.commonError: Getting the right size but the wrong sign: with the sign wrong the slopes multiply to 1, not −1, and the lines are not perpendicular.

attemptFeedback: Check that the equation satisfies every condition in the question.
supportHints: Express both slopes from standard form and impose the perpendicular relationship.

questions.prompt: Line $\ell$ is represented by ${{A}}x+{{B}}y={{C}}$. Which equation represents a line perpendicular to $\ell$ that passes through $({{x1}},{{y1}})$?

optionRationales.${{B}}x-{{A}}y={{D}}$: The slope of this line is the negative reciprocal of the given line’s slope, and the constant makes it pass through the point.
optionRationales.${{A}}x+{{B}}y={{Dpar}}$: This line keeps the given line’s coefficients, so it has the same slope: it is parallel, not perpendicular.
optionRationales.${{B}}x+{{A}}y={{D}}$: This slope is the given slope flipped over but with its sign unchanged, so the two slopes multiply to 1, not −1.
optionRationales.${{A}}x-{{B}}y={{D}}$: This slope is the opposite of the given slope but not flipped over, so the two slopes do not multiply to −1.

solutionReview.headline: Rotate the coefficient relationship for a perpendicular slope.
reasoning: A perpendicular line has slope {{B}}/{{A}}, which is represented by {{B}}x-{{A}}y=D.
Substitute the point to find D={{D}}.
solutionReview.commonError: Changing only the sign of the slope, or only flipping it; a perpendicular slope needs both, the negative reciprocal. Keeping the same coefficients gives a parallel line.
